chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Isa ibn Abdullah, who said:

Abdullah was presented with death, so his creditors gathered around him and demanded the debt owed to them. He said, 'I have no wealth with which to give to you, but be pleased with whichever you choose from the two sons of my uncle: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Ja'far.' The creditors said, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far is wealthy and delays (payment), but Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a man with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us.' [A man] with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us.

So he sent for him and informed him of the news. He said, 'I guarantee the wealth for you until harvest time,' as a show of kindness, and there was no harvest for him. The people said, 'We are pleased,' and they held him as a guarantor. When the time of harvest came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the wealth available to him, so he paid it.

key_terms.تَجَمُّلًا: As a show of kindness / gesture of goodwill

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) guarantee a debt without having wealth at the time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of *al-amanah* (trustworthiness) over material wealth, as creditors chose Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) for his truthfulness despite his lack of immediate funds. The term *tajammul* used for his promise of 'harvest' indicates a rhetorical gesture of goodwill rather than a literal expectation of agricultural yield, emphasizing reliance on divine provision (*rizq*). The narrative concludes with Allah facilitating the means for repayment, illustrating the principle that God supports those who fulfill their obligations with sincerity.
